notes:
Quick CRM notes and call snippets:
- POC summary: hosted API met latency targets (median 95ms) but cost per 1M tokens ~ $X (higher than our benchmark).
- NimbusFlow wants Dedicated for predictable unit economics and to enable caching + custom quantization profiles. Main ask: price predictability, burst capacity for campaign spikes, and a 6-month ramp option.
- Quote from CTO Samir: 'We can tolerate a weekday baseline but need predictable burst for product launches — can't be surprised by a bill spike.'
- Commercial preferences: prefer monthly commit with step-up ramps (month 1 = 40% commit, month 3 = 75%, month 6 = 100%). Finance prefers quarterly invoicing.
- Burst / overage discussion: propose 2x baseline for short windows (up to 12 hours/day) with usage pooled across region; overage to be billed at a discounted rate to committed unit price, with cap. NimbusFlow pushing for a 'grace buffer' (first 10% over commit free).
- Deployment: VPC peering required for dedicated; EU data residency for subset of customers (we recommended Private for EU residency but NimbusFlow wants Dedicated in eu-west region).
- Security: SSO/SAML in place, SOC2 required, will need KMS integration notes for procurement (they run internal HSM).
- Competitive note: evaluating Redwood vs. AtlasAI dedicated offering; Redwood strength = console + batching optimizations and transparent perf metrics.
- Risk: internal legal slow, procurement wants early-termination flexibility if product metrics don't improve in 90 days.
- Action items: finalize SOW with clear ramp schedule, define burst window policy and exact overage math, attach KMS integration appendix, confirm invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly).

pricing_discussion_summary: Customer preference: start monthly commit, move to annual on month 9
Proposed commit tiers: 250k, 500k, 1M tokens/day equivalents (converted to vGPU-hours in SOW)
Burst policy: up to 2x baseline for scheduled campaigns; automatic scaling with billing at discounted overage rate
Overage: tiered (0-10% grace, 10-50% billed at 1.25x committed rate, >50% at 1.5x) - customer requested cap at 200% of committed spend
Ramp schedule: recommended step-ups at month 1 (40%), month 3 (70%), month 6 (100%); finance requested alternate: month 1 (50%), month 4 (100%)
Discounts: multi-year / higher commit to reduce per-token price; Redwood offered an ARR-based discount ladder in draft SOW

Invoicing: prefer quarterly invoicing against committed spend; billing team awaiting confirmation
